submission.natural_language_explanation: The negative pole is this GeLU unit's resting state, saturating at the GeLU floor (~0.17): it is maximal on the first token of any input regardless of content and stays high on most ordinary tokens across domains and languages, and it is suppressed toward zero only on scattered content tokens that drive the unit's positive side (e.g. animate object nouns like 'dog'/'cat' versus 'mat', the consumption verb 'ate' versus 'cooked', food nouns like 'eggs'/'bread') or into deep inhibition (e.g. 'slowly' versus 'loudly' after 'barked'). It shows no next-token tuning (Jacobian kurtosis 3.0 with incoherent promoted/suppressed fragment lists), so the mechanism is retrospective: pole strength marks the absence of a positive-side drive in the context read so far.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Dawn fog hung over Willow Creek Farm when our volunteer bus rattled through the iron gates and coordinator Priya handed every newcomer a laminated roster with kennel assignments, coop duties, chore rotations, plus strict safety reminders. My first task meant scrubbing kennel floors while a lanky shepherd dog barked slowly from the corner run, eyeing the hose with theatrical suspicion. Beside him a nervous terrier circled its blanket, flinching whenever the metal bucket clanged against concrete. In the adjoining pen a scarred old cat kneaded a frayed cushion, purring loudly despite the surrounding chaos, while two kittens chased loose straw across the aisle. By nine the kitchen crew had cracked dozens of donated eggs into a gigantic steel bowl, whisking furiously for staff omelets. A baker from Mill Road arrived balancing wicker baskets of warm sliced bread meant for sandwiches, soup kitchens, school lunches, plus the weekend market stall. Hungry volunteers ate standing between chores, swapping stories about midnight rescues, flood evacuations, adoption paperwork, veterinary bills, grant deadlines, neighbor complaints. Priya reminded everyone that each rescued cat receives vaccinations, microchips, flea treatment, behavioral assessment, then a quiet recovery cage away from louder kennels. A shy greyhound dog arrived midmorning, ribs visible, tail tucked, trembling inside a borrowed crate lined with donated towels. Children from the village school toured the barns, scattering grain for hens, giggling as ducklings splashed through puddles near the compost heap. The cook ladled vegetable soup into tin mugs and stacked thick slices of brown bread beside a tray of boiled eggs for the lunch queue. After lunch teenagers mucked out stables, refilled water troughs, repaired a broken fence rail, then groomed ponies with stiff brushes. An elderly volunteer named Rosa handfed a toothless old dog warm mash from a chipped enamel bowl, stroking its ears while it ate. Thunder rumbled distantly and every kennelled dog barked, one beagle puppy howling slowly until Rosa calmed it with steady singing. The farrier arrived to trim hooves, hammering rhythmically while goats jostled around the feed bins and a barn cat supervised from the hayloft. Rain began spattering the tin roof, so crews dragged hay bales under tarps, covered the firewood stack, herded hens back inside the wire coop. In the farmhouse pantry, volunteers sorted jars of preserves, sacks of flour, crates of apples, wheels of cheese, bundles of herbs, bags of onions. A nutrition student demonstrated inexpensive meals, scrambling donated eggs with peppers, toasting stale bread, simmering lentils, chopping donated greens. Toddlers in the creche corner tore apart soft bread rolls, smeared them with jam, dropped crumbs everywhere, laughed when the resident terrier begged shamelessly. The terrier, a scruffy rescue named Pip, obeyed commands reluctantly, preferring to nap beneath the trestle table near warm ovens. Afternoon brought farrier invoices, delivery vans, a television crew filming the dairy herd, plus inspectors checking fences, drains, extinguishers, first aid kits. A family arrived hoping to adopt, and staff introduced a gentle Labrador dog that leaned against the father's leg, sighing contentedly during the interview. Paperwork consumed an hour: reference checks, landlord permissions, garden measurements, exercise promises, vaccination schedules, insurance quotes, microchip registrations. Meanwhile the kitchen volunteers ate cold leftovers hurriedly before the evening rush of feeding rounds, medication doses, bedding changes, final headcounts. Dusk settled as lanterns flickered along the pathways, moths swirling, owls calling from the oak copse beyond the lower meadow fence. Priya read the overnight rota aloud, assigning barn checks, foaling watch, medication alarms, gate locks, torch batteries, emergency numbers, backup contacts. Exhausted, muddy, happy, the crew gathered for cocoa, thanking farmers, drivers, donors, cooks, nurses, builders, teachers, neighbors, sponsors, friends, every helper who fed one trembling stray dog
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context saturation probe: a 500+ word farm narrative densely embedding every claimed suppressor (dog, cat, ate, eggs, bread, barked slowly) and ending on one, testing whole-context suppression.
